clue.text: Clumsy type of prick on Silver, rearing up

indicators.note: in a down clue rearing up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: both are slang for the penis, and for a fool
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Some idiot riding a silver horse that rears up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second before both are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A galoot is an awkward, oafish person, which is a clumsy type.

clue.text: (& 15dn.) Coming from Brenda's place and going down as payment to suitor?

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen; coming from her royal home is coming from her court
a building settles when it sinks into the ground

explanation.surface: A smutty royal scandal: a royal paying off a lover for sexual favours.
explanation.walkthrough: Suitor looks like a wooer, but it means one who sues. Going down is not sex but subsidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff who sues may accept money from the other side to drop the case before trial.

clue.text: Crap leader about Mail's leader is a gem

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps around the other
something crap is badly made, so the letters of the next word are messed up

parts.note: taken as written before being scrambled

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Mail

explanation.surface: A swipe at a poor newspaper editorial, with the Daily Mail's comment praised as a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader looks like a newspaper's editorial; it is the anagram fodder. The second leader means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald is a green precious stone, one kind of gem.

clue.text: Penny, surrounded by soldiers, used to remove bits of organs?

definitions.text: used to remove bits of organs?
definitions.note: a description of what the answer is for, standing for the instrument

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the armed forces are soldiers
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A woman called Penny surrounded by troops, with a grisly hint about harvesting organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are surgical pincers used to grip and pull out tissue.

clue.text: Hold nut by hair

parts.note: nut is slang for head
a lock is a strand of hair

explanation.surface: Gripping someone by the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlock is a wrestling grip that clamps the opponent's head under one arm.

clue.text: Hoover against Bill getting united twice with Monica's top

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
U is the abbreviation for united, taken two times

indicators.note: the top of a word written down is its opening letter, so only the first of Monica is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Monica

explanation.surface: A dig at Bill Clinton and Monica Lewinsky, with J. Edgar Hoover lined up against the president.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover looks like the FBI chief opposing Bill Clinton, but it is the verb for cleaning a carpet; Bill is just an account.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the brand name Hoover is the everyday verb for cleaning with a suction cleaner, the same action as to vacuum.

clue.text: Little St. Edmund's performance assessing body

indicators.note: little asks for the short form of the name, so the end of Edmund is cut off

parts.note: the possessive 's can be rewritten as of
the saint's abbreviation as written
the full name before shortening

explanation.surface: Sounds like a school play at a little school called St Edmund's being judged.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed is the usual nickname for Edmund. Ofsted is the English government office that inspects and grades schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Ofsted, the Office for Standards in Education, inspects schools and rates how well they perform.

clue.text: (& 26dn.) A sailor who's experienced a dose screwed good

indicators.note: screwed means twisted up, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written before twisting
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sailor who has caught a venereal disease and been well and truly screwed.
explanation.walkthrough: A dose is slang for a sexually transmitted infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old, seasoned seaman.

clue.text: (see 11ac.)
In which Bush gets around wrecking of career no.1

indicators.note: wrecking means smashing up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the numeral one looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: George W. Bush travels about while his career goes down in flames.
explanation.definitionFit: Air Force One is the call sign of the plane carrying the US president, then Bush.

clue.text: (& 9dn.) Something taken by chance — seized by the publicity-seeking politician

definitions.note: the clue's opening 'Something' does double duty: the definition is something seized by such a politician

parts.note: a picture is something you take with a camera
a chance is an opening or occasion

explanation.surface: Something snatched by luck, grabbed by a politician hungry for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash separates the wordplay from a descriptive definition; politicians are famous for grabbing any chance to be pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged chance to be pictured by the press is exactly what a publicity-hungry politician grabs.

clue.text: Dick starts to itch, inevitably leading to tragedy

parts.note: Dick is a pet form of the name Richard

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the initials of the next two words are used

parts.note: the opening letters of itch and inevitably

explanation.surface: A crude joke: an itchy member is bound to end in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick reads as the rude slang word, but it is just the nickname for Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's play about the deposed king is titled The Tragedy of King Richard the Second.

clue.text: Eye's description of drunken sot getting out of post-coital embarrassment

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters of sot may come in any order
embarrassment means confusion, so what is left gets scrambled
getting out of means leaving, so those letters depart from the longer word

parts.note: the three letters to remove, in whatever order they appear
taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: Private Eye describing a drunk sneaking off after an embarrassing one-night stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Eye looks like the magazine, but it is the organ of sight. The letters S, O, T come out of POSTCOITAL and the remaining seven are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical is the adjective for anything relating to sight or the eye.

clue.text: Withdraw beer, getting queasy

parts.note: British slang for beer or weak drink
feeling off means feeling unwell

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the pub because the beer is turning their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang piss is crude for alcohol, and feeling off means feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Piss off is a crude British way to say go away, that is, to leave or retreat.

clue.text: (see 2dn.)
(& 20ac.) Nice place according to agents involved in Grade's resignation

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Michael Grade quitting the BBC, with spies saying something about a spot in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice looks like the French city, but it means pleasant. Michael Grade left the BBC chair for ITV in 2006.
explanation.definitionFit: Des res, short for desirable residence, is estate agents' jargon for an attractive home.

clue.text: Bush type, extremely lacking, developed fever

indicators.note: developed suggests growth into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
lacking its extremes means the very first and very last letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written, as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A Bush kind of man, short of something, comes down with a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes are the B of Bush and the E of type, leaving USHTYP to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhus is an infectious disease spread by lice, marked by a high temperature.

clue.text: Stupid git dunked in buckets of old Chinese men's hair?

indicators.note: dunked in means dropped inside, so one group goes into another

parts.note: pails are buckets

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written before being jumbled

explanation.surface: A fool is dunked headfirst in buckets, with an odd question about hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Git is British slang for an unpleasant fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the Qing dynasty Chinese men wore a long plait called a queue, a type of pigtail; the question mark flags it as an example.

clue.text: A drag penetrating senior fuel-feeder

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senior
a drag on a cigarette or joint is a toke

explanation.surface: Someone taking a puff on a joint in front of an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker shovels coal into a furnace or boiler, keeping it supplied with fuel.

clue.text: (see 16ac.)
Counter-revolution, one of several that did Gore no good

definitions.text: one of several that did Gore no good

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A political backlash, like the ballots that went against Al Gore.
explanation.walkthrough: Counter-revolution reads as a political term, but it splits into the word and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida ballots were counted again several times in 2000, and Gore still lost the presidency.

clue.text: By which perverse natural state bastards rule?

definitions.note: describes the principle that things naturally go wrong

parts.note: sod is mild British slang for an unpleasant person
a rule is a law

explanation.surface: A perverse land where the bastards are in power.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a country and rule like government; the clue's whole reading also hints the answer, since this principle lets the worst happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod's law is the British name for the jokey principle that things go wrong at the worst moment, like Murphy's law.

clue.text: Getting thing out, that is a bedtime habit

indicators.note: something put out of shape is no longer in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A flasher's routine of getting his thing out before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit reads as a routine, but it also means a garment, as in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a garment, or habit, worn to bed.

clue.text: Allowed a break from work? Playing? Sod off!

parts.note: a show that is on is being played or performed
sod off is a crude order to leave

explanation.surface: A worker asking for time off is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod off is mild British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on leave has been granted official time away from their job.

clue.text: Potential lifesaver when Blair, losing 40% lead, gets sack

indicators.note: losing the leading two fifths means the first two of five letters are dropped

parts.note: Tony Blair, taken as written
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: Tony Blair slips in the polls and is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack reads as dismissal, but here it is a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's airbag inflates in a crash to cushion occupants and can save lives.

clue.text: What blubber makes of hacks around dive

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside another

parts.note: hacks as a verb means cuts or rips, which tears also means
a dive is a sudden fall or drop

explanation.surface: A whale's fat, or a jibe at what crying journalists do after a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Blubber looks like whale fat; here it is someone who blubbers, or cries noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A person crying sheds drops of water from the eyes, so tears are what a weeper produces.

clue.text: (see 8dn.)
Ex-rock group member entertains right plonker

indicators.note: a host entertains guests inside, so one letter goes within the name

parts.note: Keith Moon, drummer of The Who, who died in 1978
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A former rock star playing host to a right idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insults for a stupid person, so one is a synonym of the other.

clue.text: Prescott's beginning to pull (cool!) and make a connection

indicators.note: the beginning of a name is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Prescott
to lug is to drag or haul
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: John Prescott, Labour deputy prime minister, trying his luck at pulling women.
explanation.walkthrough: Pull is British slang for seducing someone, but here it means haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug in is to connect a device to the mains by its plug.

clue.text: Cancel entertaining Labour's no. 2, flower!

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: to annul is to cancel

indicators.note: number two picks out the second letter of the word before it

parts.note: the second letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A call to scrap something while hosting Labour's deputy leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour's no. 2 looks like John Prescott, the party's deputy, but it is the second letter of the word. Flower here really is a bloom, not the usual crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a plant, such as many bedding flowers, that completes its life cycle in one year.
